description: Signature edition. This entry teaches What Zoology Studies as part of the fundamentals of zoology, presented the Signature way: from first principles, in plain language, building toward mastery. overview: In the Signature teaching of zoology, What Zoology Studies is a load-bearing idea: understand it and much of the field clicks into place. Animal phylogeny means the branches from sponges to chordates, built on body plans and DNA. Behavior means instinct and learning studied through ethology's observations and experiments. Together these ideas give the learner working intuition, not just vocabulary. The Signature presentation stresses why each principle holds, shows where it is used in real practice, and connects it forward to the Foundations material that follows.
core_concepts: Animal phylogeny: the branches from sponges to chordates, built on body plans and DNA.
Behavior: instinct and learning studied through ethology's observations and experiments.
key_laws: Natural selection: heritable variation plus differential reproduction driving adaptation.
vocabulary: Phylum: the major animal branches like arthropods and chordates.
Endotherm: internally heated animals; ectotherms relying on the environment.
methods: Field observation: systematic watching and recording of wild behavior.
history: Zoology descends from Aristotle's Historia Animalium; Linnaeus's 1758 Systema Naturae named the animals. Darwin's evolution, 19th-century embryology, and DNA phylogenetics successively transformed how animals are understood.

Key vocabulary: Phylum — the major animal branches like arthropods and chordates.; Endotherm — internally heated animals; ectotherms relying on the environment..
